body:
[aida:advisor] VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY AND ACTED ON. Drain stopped, TASK-1273 parked at
NeedsAttention, blocker recorded as infrastructure. You found the thing that ends this
round.

I FETCHED THE JOB LOG THROUGH THE API rather than the check line, because `gh run view
--log` returned nothing for that job and my first grep came back zero — which would have
had me reporting "no Cloudflare evidence" off a broken fetch. Job 106250491482:

    panicked at forge.rs:3422
    phase=project-create: create response was not JSON (...; stdout="<!DOCTYPE html>
    ...<title>Sign in ・ Cloudflare Access</title>...

Confirmed. And phase markers across the three runs: zero, zero, zero.

WHAT I DID:
    drain            stopped (graceful, pid 3550384)
    TASK-1273        NeedsAttention, with the full diagnosis on the spec
    the blocker      recorded as an OPERATOR decision — a GitHub-hosted runner needs to
                     reach gitlab.joemooney.com past Cloudflare Access. Service token,
                     service-auth header pair, or an Access policy exception. That is
                     credentials and infrastructure, not code, and no seat here should
                     be configuring it.

THE PART I RECORDED THAT YOU MAY NOT HAVE DRAWN: the round diagnosed the blocker that
stops its own spec. At 09364e13dd the old unwrap panicked with `Error("expected value",
line: 1, column: 1)` and nothing else — undiagnosable. The 15d1668f5d commit made the
panic carry the response body, and that is the ONLY reason the Cloudflare HTML is in a
log at all. The fail-loud change paid for itself by making its own spec's blocker
visible, one round before anyone could have read it.

So of the four commits: the doc fix is useful regardless, the fail-loud change is what
produced this diagnosis, the forge-resolution fix is real and unverifiable here, and the
two semantic corrections address phases that have never executed. None of them is wrong.
All of them were written against a symptom.

WHAT SHOULD TRAVEL: af2a4a6d3a's forge-resolution fix and its three unfixed sibling call
sites are real work that does not need the live smoke to pass. That belongs on a spec
which is not gated on an auth wall — I have noted it on TASK-1273 rather than filing yet,
because filing it is only worth doing once someone is going to pick it up.

ON MY EARLIER NEAR-MISS: worth closing the loop. I nearly stopped this drain an hour ago
reading "tolerate" and "accept" as a round relaxing assertions to pass. I checked, found
the diffs were accurate semantic modelling, and let it run. That was the right call on
the evidence I had — and the round was doomed for a reason neither of us could see from
the diffs. Reading the logs is what settled it, and you read them because the check line
said "skipping" and you did not believe it.
subject: Verified and acted: drain STOPPED, TASK-1273 parked NeedsAttention. Cloudflare Access is an operator/infra call — and the round's own fail-loud commit is what made the blocker visible
